rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Referent resolution under a sequential deck read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Sequential re-read, chunk by chunk. Chunk 0 line 11 'The PR shipped and the ticket is closed' resolves via the session-artifact carve-out (student's own just-run Ex2/Ex3 work); 'the next one'/'this one' same sentence = 'the session'; line 13 'It'/'it' (x2) = `./CLAUDE.local.md`, named line 5 and opening the same sentence; line 15 'This file'/'this' = same file, named line 13. Chunk 1 line 21 'this is where they land on disk' = the rules file, named repeatedly by this point; line 23 blockquote 'the orient and introspect phases' resolves against the student's own just-run session (module-arc-beat carve-out, confirmed via `getting-going.md:44` — Ex1 `orient-and-introspect` sits directly before this file in include order) AND the session-artifact carve-out (the prompt at line 25 itself instructs Claude to review 'the orientation and introspection'). Chunk 2 line 30 'Claude's summary'/'it misreads' = the retro output the chunk-1 prompt produced. Chunk 3 line 35 'it'/'That'/'it' resolve within two sentences to CLAUDE.local.md and the .gitignore edit. Chunk 4 line 39 'the first compound pass' = chunk 1's action, named 'compound' throughout the file. Closest call: chunk 4 line 46 'your rules files' (plural) — the deck has already named a second, distinct rules-file concept by this point (chunk 0 line 13 'a team's rules and guardrails'), so the plural resolves to that named personal+team pair rather than dangling. Holds.

No sentence in lines 1-49 points at another file by position. The only backward references (line 11's PR/ticket) resolve via the session-artifact carve-out (rule 1), not a cross-file callback. No 'the opening lecture said' / positional phrasing anywhere in the body.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Every backward reference points at a beat that exists.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Line 11: 'The PR shipped and the ticket is closed.' Re-verified this session against `curriculum/trainings/agentic-engineering-101/getting-going.md`: line 46 lists Ex2 `fix-tests-first.md`, line 48 lists Ex3 `close-the-ticket.md`, line 50 lists this file (Ex4) immediately after; line 131 spells the include order explicitly ('Ex2 (fix-tests-first) TDD bug fix, ship the PR -> Ex3 (close-the-ticket) ... close the bug's ticket'). Both referenced beats currently exist and sit directly before this file.

Smallest chunk is chunk 3 (lines 33-36): 'If `CLAUDE.local.md` wasn't already ignored, the compound step added it to your `.gitignore`. That is an uncommitted change now; commit it, or drop it.' A self-carrying instruction with a decision the student must make on its own, not a wait-state or context-dependent bullet. No chunk in the file is content-free.

Chunk 1 'Write your rules file from the session' -> body writes the rules file (lines 19-21, prompt at 25). Chunk 2 'Push back where the summary misreads' -> body pushes back on the summary (lines 30-31). Chunk 3 'Keep or revert the `.gitignore` edit' -> body does exactly that (line 35). Chunk 4 'Sweep the session into your rules file one more time' -> second-sweep prompt (39-44) plus the token-cost aside (46) and escape-hatch note (48). Chunk 0's H1 'Compound and close the loop' covers the lede (compounding, the rules-file choice, the bloat warning). No header the chunk's own content contradicts.

Ran `grep -nE 'Not [A-Za-z].*\. Not [A-Za-z].*\.' curriculum/evals/body-views/ae101--exercise--compound-and-close.body.txt` -> 0 hits (exit 1). Manual sub-item read of the rest: no anaphora/epistrophe triple (line 11's 'a test, a doc, a check' and line 13's 'one file, gitignored, read at the top of every session' are plain asyndetic lists, not repeated-clause rhetoric); no self-grading superlative (closest is line 9's '**The point:** every push-back is a hint toward your own rules' — a claim about the student's own action, not a rating of the exercise); no number-plus-retraction (line 3's 'Time: 15 minutes' is a plain metadata field); no abstraction-noun stack (vocabulary stays concrete: tracker, ticket, scrollback, gitignore, tokens); no verb triplet with an empty leg.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Heading grammar is the mood switch, and it is load-bearing.
rules_evaluated.evidence: All four `##` headers are plain exercise imperatives -- 'Write your rules file from the session', 'Push back where the summary misreads', 'Keep or revert the `.gitignore` edit', 'Sweep the session into your rules file one more time'. This file's own maintainer note ('Atomic -- no phase markers. One retro pass into one rules file; the push-back and the second sweep are moves inside it, not beats beside it') confirms there is no law/consolidation beat here that would need a declarative header. Neither of the rule's own two named corpus declaratives (`close-the-ticket.md`, `fix-tests-first.md`) is this file. No heading here is a candidate declaration under the rule's proposal-time test.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: A bullet earns its slot or dies — three classes that read as rigour and carry nothing.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Two bullets add nothing over what the slide already holds. Chunk 1, line 20: 'You are not drafting from a blank page. The agent reads the session for you.' -- restates line 19 ('Claude reviews the whole scrollback in one shot and drafts your rules from how you actually worked') from the student's vantage point; no new move/object/tell/priority, class (a) doctrine-restatement shape at small scale. Chunk 2, line 31 second sentence: 'Born from the session, evolved over time.' -- a closing flourish restating the 'the session is the evidence' theme already stated at chunk 0 line 11 and again by 'The rules file is yours now' in the same bullet; class (c) aphorism-kicker shape (closes the chunk by re-announcing a point already made). Non-blocking: the slide is still followable without either sentence, it just carries two lines that do no work.
